Trigger.dev is an open source background jobs framework that lets you write reliable workflows in plain async code. Run long-running AI tasks, handle complex background jobs...No timeouts, elastic scaling
This triggers the task and returns a handle...You can use the handle to check the status of the task, cancel and retry it.
This task will retry 10 times with exponential backoff.
Scheduled tasks are only for recurring tasks...A task that is triggered on a recurring schedule using cron syntax.
Waitpoint tokens pause task runs until you complete the token. They're commonly used for approval workflows and other scenarios where you need to wait for external confirmation
When a task run starts it is locked to the latest version of the code (for that environment). Once locked it won't change versions, even if you deploy new versions.
You can set the concurrency limit for a task by setting the `concurrencyLimit` property on the task's queue. This limits the number of runs that can be executing at any one time
You can view your current limits, quotas, and rate limit usage in real-time by visiting the **Limits** page in the dashboard
A run can go through **various** states during its lifecycle...Pending version...Delayed...Queued...Dequeued...Executing
Get live run updates and stream data from background tasks to your frontend or backend. No polling.
The Trigger.dev MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server enables AI assistants to interact directly with your Trigger.dev projects.
Durable multi-turn AI chats — one Trigger.dev task per conversation, surviving refreshes, deploys, and crashes.
The Trigger.dev MCP server includes tools for having conversations with your chat agents directly from AI coding tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and others.
Install Trigger.dev agent skills to teach any AI coding assistant how to write tasks, realtime frontends, and chat.agent AI agents.
The Trigger.dev CLI has a number of options and commands to help you develop locally, self host, and deploy your tasks.
Self-hosting Trigger.dev means you run and manage the platform on your own infrastructure, giving you full control over your environment, deployment process, and the URLs you expose the service on.
This simple GitHub action workflow will deploy your Trigger.dev tasks when new code is pushed to the `main` branch.
